calibration.evidence: run kv-tier/host-pool2 on flashnext-4gpu (91 GiB host): host pool 9 GiB + host KV tier 12 GiB left 4 GiB available and served (post-fill prefill 1,901 -> 3,165 tok/s, KV-loan collapse avoided); a 32 GiB tier with the n-gram table on disk left 0 GiB available, refused
the 4 GiB that served on a 91 GiB host is 4.4% of MemTotal; 5% scales that margin to larger hosts

run tail-size on flashnext-4gpu: the 8 GiB tail point (64% backing) keeps decode within 1% of the smallest tail (361 vs 364 tok/s) and TTFT at 1.67 s, with 8-session prefill +4% (2,520 vs 2,422 tok/s); balanced takes about 60%

reproduces today's launch (no regression): with the 9 GiB host pool and the 12 GiB host KV tier the engine auto-sized 43 snapshots of 112.48 MiB (4.72 GiB) of a want of 72 (9 a sequence for 8 x 262144 at a 4096 interval), the tier having been placed first (run rsc03-plan step 2, 2026-11-02); with the tier off it sized all 72 (7.91 GiB, run host-pool); planning the want first would itself change today's behaviour

today's launch (HOST_KV_MIB=12288): the 9 GiB pool plus a 12 GiB tier took post-fill prefill from 1,901 to 3,165 tok/s (the KV-loan collapse avoided), and 6-stream decode after an ~1M-token session fill from 52.8 to 46.9 ms a step, with the n-gram table kept in RAM; a 32 GiB tier (n-gram table on disk) left 0 GiB free and is refused by the reserve

RSC08 S3 hardware gate on the Flash-Next layout (runs/rsc08-s3-gate): with the helpers' and the engine's start-up memory counted, the host still lost 273 and about 280 MiB between the manifest write and the engine's own host-room check in three of four starts; one start planned to 75 MiB spare fell 205 MiB short at that check and stopped. 1024 MiB is about 3.6 x the largest observed unexplained loss, chosen as a safety ratio (a judgement, not a derivation); the refit replaces it (RSC03: a start that fails the engine's host-room check stores its observed shortfall with the cache entry and retries once with the margin raised to it)
